definitions.explanation: A business or trade that has been passed down through a family, typically across generations. Refers to the occupation that defines a family's livelihood.

examples.english: To take over the family business.

examples.japanese: {父|ちち}の{家業|かぎょう}は{豆腐|とうふ}{屋|や}だった。
examples.english: My father's family business was a tofu shop.

examples.japanese: {長男|ちょうなん}は{家業|かぎょう}を{継|つ}がずに{東京|とうきょう}で{会社員|かいしゃいん}になった。
examples.english: The eldest son didn't take over the family business and became a company employee in Tokyo.

notes:
USAGE:
The most common collocation is {家業|かぎょう}を{継|つ}ぐ (to take over the family business). In traditional Japanese society, the eldest son was expected to inherit the {家業|かぎょう}, but this expectation has weakened in modern times.

COLLOCATIONS:
- {家業|かぎょう}を{継|つ}ぐ — to take over the family business
- {家業|かぎょう}を{手伝|てつだ}う — to help with the family business
- {家業|かぎょう}を{営|いとな}む — to run the family business
- {代々|だいだい}の{家業|かぎょう} — family business passed down for generations

CULTURAL NOTE:
Many traditional Japanese businesses — such as {旅館|りょかん} (inns), {酒蔵|さかぐら} (sake breweries), and {和菓子|わがし}{店|てん} (Japanese sweet shops) — are {家業|かぎょう} that have been handed down for centuries.
